message.content:
The most conspicuous dominant genetic trait in lions is the **presence of the mane in adult males**.  
This trait is governed by a dominant allele of the androgen‑receptor (AR) gene, which drives the development of the mane’s dense, dark fur and associated secondary sexual characteristics.
